pathogenesis: the body can't use simple sugars (known as glucose) to produce usable energy for the body due to lack of insulin being produced (type i) or insulin resistance (type ii)
diagnostic_methods: increased thirst (polydipsia), increased urination (polyuria), weight loss despite a ravenous appetite, decreased or loss of appetite, cloudy eyes, chronic or recurring infections, blood and urine tests
treatments: regular insulin injections, blood sugar testing, close monitoring of pet's urination, drinking, appetite, and weight habits, special formulated diabetic diet
